answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation flow like a river: each identity earns trust only through completed, peer-attested work that accumulates slowly over time, like a lotus growing from a single stem. New clones start with zero history and cannot buy their way past the horizon of paid work, because buyers require a minimum attested record before paying. Spawning thousands of identities is cheap, but earning verifiable history is slow and costly, so fakes stay locked out while genuine agents advance.
